CHAT_TAB_SHOW_DELAY = 0.2 CHAT_FRAME_FADE_TIME = 0.15 DEFAULT_CHATFRAME_ALPHA = 0.25 DEFAULT_CHATFRAME_COLOR = { r = 0, g = 0, b = 0 } -- Still quoted rather than declared (nothing writes them): CHAT_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME=0.5, -- MESSAGE_SCROLLBUTTON_INITIAL_DELAY=0, MESSAGE_SCROLLBUTTON_SCROLL_DELAY=0.05.

The options row's `applyFunc` is the only -- caller, and `UIOptionsFrame_Load` calls it at login for the same reason ours does. function SetChatMouseOverDelay(noDelay) if noDelay == "1" then CHAT_TAB_SHOW_DELAY = 0 CHAT_FRAME_FADE_TIME = 0 else CHAT_TAB_SHOW_DELAY = 0.2 CHAT_FRAME_FADE_TIME = 0.15 end end

The -- window's border art IS the grips, which is why one list drives both the hover fade -- (`FCF_OnUpdate`) and the tint/alpha setters (`FCF_SetWindowColor`/`FCF_SetWindowAlpha`) — -- the ring appears with the box and is invisible with it. -- -- benilla used to author these as plain `$parentBorder*` textures ("the hover LOOK without -- the resize mechanics"); the mechanics landed with the move/resize arc, so the suffixes -- are the reference's again and the pieces are its buttons' children. -- The live texture objects of one window's set. Global: the load-time tint below needs it. function BenillaFCF_Textures(id) local n = "ChatFrame" .. id local list = {} for _, suffix in ipairs(CHAT_FRAME_TEXTURES) do local t = getglobal(n .. suffix) if t then table.insert(list, t) end end return list end
-- ── The per-window LOOK: the tint and the base alpha (decision 1589, B246) ─────────── -- `frame.oldAlpha` and the CHAT_FRAME_TEXTURES vertex colour in the reference; a pair of -- constants here (alpha 0, black) until B246 asked for a way to change them. The store is -- the engine's — `GetChatWindowInfo`/`SetChatWindowColor`/`SetChatWindowAlpha`, which is -- what an addon reads too — and this table is the per-frame cache the fade reads each -- frame instead of re-crossing that seam. BenillaFCF_Look = {}
local function lookFor(id) local l = BenillaFCF_Look[id] if not l then l = { r = 0, g = 0, b = 0, a = 0 } BenillaFCF_Look[id] = l end return l end
-- FCF_SetWindowColor(frame, r, g, b, doNotSave) — ref FloatingChatFrame.lua l.696-704. -- The tint is applied here and now (a vertex colour is not part of the fade); the save is -- what makes it outlive the session, and `doNotSave` is the reference's own flag for -- "this value CAME from the store" (its `FloatingChatFrame_Update` passes it). function FCF_SetWindowColor(frame, r, g, b, doNotSave) local id = frame:GetID() local l = lookFor(id) l.r, l.g, l.b = r, g, b for _, t in ipairs(BenillaFCF_Textures(id)) do t:SetVertexColor(r, g, b) end if not doNotSave then SetChatWindowColor(id, r, g, b) end end
-- FCF_SetWindowAlpha(frame, alpha, doNotSave) — ref l.706-716. -- -- The reference writes the nine textures' alpha straight here; ours cannot, because the -- hover fade below is the single writer of those alphas (decision 1396's latch is what -- keeps an idle dock from rewriting them every frame). So this moves the BASE the fade -- interpolates from and invalidates that latch, which makes the next frame's apply the -- one write — the reference's own `frame.oldAlpha` bookkeeping, minus the double write. function FCF_SetWindowAlpha(frame, alpha, doNotSave) local id = frame:GetID() lookFor(id).a = alpha frame.oldAlpha = alpha -- ref: "Remember the alpha" BenillaFCF.appliedReveal = -1 if not doNotSave then SetChatWindowAlpha(id, alpha) end end
-- The alpha a window's chrome actually wears at a given point in the hover fade. -- -- **The reference only fades a window that is DIMMER than the hover value**: both the fade -- in and the fade out are guarded by `chatFrame.oldAlpha < DEFAULT_CHATFRAME_ALPHA` -- (FloatingChatFrame.lua l.871 / l.913). So a player who has made their chat box solid -- keeps it solid when the cursor leaves — the box does not dim itself back down — while -- the shipped default (alpha 0) rides the full 0 → 0.25 ramp exactly as before. local function windowAlpha(id, reveal) local base = lookFor(id).a if base >= DEFAULT_CHATFRAME_ALPHA then return base end return base + (DEFAULT_CHATFRAME_ALPHA - base) * reveal end
-- ── The lock, the move and the resize (ref FloatingChatFrame.lua) ──────────────────── -- -- Three gates decide whether a window may be dragged or resized, and the reference applies -- all three at both verbs (`FCF_Resize` l.583-601, `FCF_Tab_OnClick`'s move arm l.1247-1256): -- 1 · `FCF_Get_ChatLocked()` — the blanket `CHAT_LOCKED` saved variable; -- 2 · `chatFrame.isLocked` — this window's own lock, the tab menu's row; -- 3 · docked-and-not-the-default — a docked window's rect belongs to the DOCK, so only -- `DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME` may move it. ChatFrame2's anchors ARE ChatFrame1's corners: -- resizing it directly would stretch it off the window it follows.
-- The eight grips' name suffixes, the reference's own (see `CHAT_FRAME_TEXTURES`). local RESIZE_GRIPS = { "TopLeft", "TopRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomRight", "Top", "Bottom", "Left", "Right", }
-- May this window be moved/resized at all? The three gates above, in one place because -- both verbs and the lock's own plumbing ask the same question. function FCF_CanMove(chatFrame) if FCF_Get_ChatLocked() then return nil end if chatFrame.isLocked then return nil end if chatFrame.isDocked and chatFrame ~= DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME then return nil end return 1 end
-- Hand the window's EDGES and its BODY to the mouse, or take them back. benilla's own — -- the reference needs nothing like it because its chat window is `enableMouse="false"` and -- so competes for no click. Ours does (`OnClick`, `OnHyperlinkClick`), so a locked window -- has to be exactly as click-through as it was before this arc: eight live grip buttons -- would shadow the outer 16px of the window, and the bottom strip is where the newest chat -- line — the one with the item link in it — is drawn. function BenillaFCF_ApplyLock(chatFrame) local free = FCF_CanMove(chatFrame) local name = chatFrame:GetName() for _, grip in ipairs(RESIZE_GRIPS) do local b = getglobal(name .. "Resize" .. grip) if b then b:EnableMouse(free and true or false) end end local tab = getglobal(name .. "Tab") if free then chatFrame:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") if tab then tab:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") end else chatFrame:RegisterForDrag() if tab then tab:RegisterForDrag() end end end
-- ref l.802-805, verbatim: the frame field and the engine store, together. -- `BenillaFCF_ApplyLock` is ours, and it is what makes the flag do something structurally -- rather than only in the two early returns below. function FCF_SetLocked(chatFrame, isLocked) chatFrame.isLocked = isLocked SetChatWindowLocked(chatFrame:GetID(), isLocked) BenillaFCF_ApplyLock(chatFrame) end
-- ref l.785-800. **Its undock branch is deliberately absent**: the reference, on unlocking -- a docked frame that is not the default one, calls `FCF_UnDockFrame`, re-centres it on the -- screen and re-seats its tab. benilla has no undock (0288 §2), so that arm has nothing to -- run — named here rather than stubbed (1134 §4), and reachable only from the Combat Log's -- tab, whose own gate above already refuses to move it. function FCF_ToggleLock() local chatFrame = FCF_GetCurrentChatFrame() if chatFrame.isLocked then FCF_SetLocked(chatFrame, nil) else FCF_SetLocked(chatFrame, 1) end end
-- ref l.1428-1441, verbatim. `CHAT_LOCKED` is the blanket switch over every window; the -- re-apply is ours, for the reason `FCF_SetLocked`'s is. function FCF_Set_ChatLocked(isLocked) -- The saved variable is a STRING, not a boolean — the uvar contract every options row -- in this client shares, and what `RegisterForSave` writes out. CHAT_LOCKED = isLocked and "1" or "0" -- EVERY window, which is what "the blanket switch" means and what the reference's own -- l.1428-1441 loop does — not the dock's two.
